outcomes.name: PXE parity
outcomes.text: PXE provisioning runs on the Mac app alone: x86 machines boot from the network and come back as named hosts online in Viam with nobody at a console, and the server Mac holds nothing but the app.
outcomes.signal: on a Mac with no Python, Docker, Homebrew or dnsmasq, after the one-time BIOS setup, a PXE batch of ten reaches installed and shows online at app.viam.com, with no monitor or keyboard attached during the run

outcomes.name: Media from any Mac
outcomes.text: Any client Mac flashes SD cards for queued Pis and USB sticks for queued x86 machines, and each machine comes back as a named host online in Viam with nobody at a console.
outcomes.signal: on a Mac other than the server, a provisioner flashes an SD card for a queued Pi and a USB stick for a queued x86 machine; both machines boot from them, reach installed and show online at app.viam.com

outcomes.name: Server setup
outcomes.text: Someone trusted to run a server on the shop's LAN sets one up by installing the app and turning on server mode; the app chooses the interface and fetches the ISO and boot files, without a terminal.
outcomes.signal: on a fresh Mac, someone goes from downloading the app to a server that answers a PXE machine, without opening a terminal

outcomes.name: Unattended server
outcomes.text: The server runs unattended: it comes back on every boot with nobody logged in, a crashed service restarts on its own, and the server's keeper sees and controls each service from the menu bar.
outcomes.signal: after the server Mac reboots, a client on another device reaches the server before anyone logs in; when the keeper logs in, the menu bar shows both services running, and turning one off and back on there takes effect

outcomes.name: Provision from any Mac
outcomes.text: A provisioner sets up environments and provisions batches from their own Mac, without a terminal or access to the server Mac.
outcomes.signal: a provisioner who never touched the server Mac creates an environment and provisions a batch that reaches installed, without opening a terminal

outcomes.name: Watch a batch
outcomes.text: A provisioner watches a batch from the app on their own Mac or iPhone: each machine shows the stage it is in, and a failed machine says where it stopped and why within minutes of stalling.
outcomes.signal: in a batch with one machine unplugged mid-download, the app on a provisioner's Mac and on their iPhone each shows every machine's stage as it advances; the rest reach installed, and the unplugged one fails within minutes naming the ISO-download stage

outcomes.name: Camera binding
outcomes.text: At the rack, a provisioner binds machines to queue slots with an iPhone's camera.
outcomes.signal: with only an iPhone, a provisioner binds each machine in a batch to its slot by camera, and each machine provisions as the one bound to it

outcomes.name: Fire and forget
outcomes.text: Provisioners fire and forget: they start a batch and walk away, sure they'll hear when machines are ready and when one needs them.
outcomes.signal: a provisioner starts a batch and quits the app; without opening it again, they are notified on their Mac or iPhone when the batch is ready, and within minutes when one machine fails, with its stage and reason
